title: AI Slop Detector
description: Edits AI-written copy so it stops reading like AI. Blog posts, LinkedIn posts, newsletters, landing pages, bios, sales emails, case studies — finds every generic phrase and makes it sound like a person actually wrote it.

title: The Brain Unclogger
description: Dump everything in your head. It sorts it into do, decide, delegate, remember and ignore, without turning every thought into another task.
keywords: Do Decide Delegate Remember Ignore When your brain is full and you can't tell what's urgent anymore. Before you try to plan the week. When ideas are living in 14 tabs, three Notes files and a Slack message to yourself. Your brain dump sorted into do, decide, delegate, remember and ignore. The decisions pulled out on their own. An ignore pile you're allowed to actually ignore.

title: Build Your Own Skill
description: Turns any workflow you repeat into a complete, working Claude skill file — written out and ready to save. Weekly reports, recurring reviews, monthly documents, checklists that live in your head, prompts you keep retyping. Package it once, use it forever.

title: Communicate Like a CEO
description: Rewrites and coaches any workplace communication so it lands the way an executive needs it — status updates, Slack messages to leadership, emails to clients, project updates, escalations, budget requests, performance reviews.

title: Coordinator to Owner
description: Turns someone trusted with tasks into someone trusted with outcomes. For coordinators, EAs, associates, analysts, specialists, and team leads whose work is good but scope isn't growing. The "why am I not getting promoted" skill.

title: Delegation Brief
description: Writes the handoff brief that makes delegated work come back right the first time. Briefing direct reports, contractors, agencies, peers on leave cover, or onboarding a new hire onto a recurring task — stops the "that's not what I asked for" loop.

title: Just Decide Already
description: For when you've researched something to death. It compares your options, exposes which criteria actually matter, calls out false distinctions and forces a decision.
keywords: You've got a comparison spreadsheet and still no answer. You keep reopening a decision you already made. The two or three criteria that actually matter. Which differences between the options aren't real. A decision framework that ends in a choice.

title: Learning Curve Destroyer
description: Turns Claude into a ruthless, time-boxed teacher whose only objective is making you FUNCTIONAL in a skill before your time budget runs out. Not educated. Not well-rounded. Functional. Delivers a plan, a first drill, and a proof you can do the thing.

title: Logic Police
description: Finds what's WRONG with an idea, offer, pitch, plan, or strategy before a customer, investor, regulator, or the market finds it. Uses rotating adversarial personas — skeptical CFO, angry customer, burned-out journalist — and tags every hole by severity.

title: The Meeting Before the Meeting
description: Prep for an important meeting: what matters, what you need to know, what to ask, what could derail it and what decision should actually get made.
keywords: What matters What you need to know What you need to ask What could derail the meeting What decision should actually get made Before a meeting you can't afford to wing. When there's a decision in the room and nobody has said what it is. A short prep sheet: what matters, what to know, what to ask, what could go sideways. The decision the meeting should actually make, in one sentence.

title: Meetings That Earn Their Hour
description: Runs meetings that produce decisions — and kills the ones that don't. Agendas, pre-reads, recaps, action items, recurring meeting audits, declines, reschedules. Turns status meetings that should be documents into documents.

title: Research It So I Don't Have To
description: Researches something thoroughly, then gives you only what matters: what changed the answer, the tradeoffs, the open questions and what to do next.
keywords: What matters What changed the answer Tradeoffs Recommendation criteria Unresolved questions What to do next You need to understand something well enough to decide, and you don't have six hours. You're comparing things to buy, book or sign up for. A short answer with the tradeoffs, not a report. The questions nobody could answer yet. What to do next.

title: Tell Me What I'm Missing
description: Give it a plan, decision or idea. It challenges your assumptions, finds what's missing and points out what you stopped questioning because you already like the idea.
keywords: Right after you've decided something and feel great about it. Before you take a plan to anyone who can say no. When everyone you've asked agrees with you. The three assumptions most likely to make it fail. The information you don't have yet. The risks you've been skating past. What evidence would change the conclusion.
